title: HELMET PROTOCOL: Granulation tissue as Dura autologous-graft. Model in Wistar Rats
protocol: Insert Sylastic® plates subcutaneously in the dorsal interscapular region after making a 1 cm incision.
Perform preoperative fasting for 12 hours before surgery.
Administer ketamine anesthesia with a dose of 30 mg/kg IM or 12 mg/kg IM.
Inject xylazine at a dose of 3 mg/kg to achieve Stage 3: Level 2 anesthesia.
Monitor the animal's plantar reflex to confirm optimal anesthesia levels.
Maintain body temperature using 100 watt lamps placed 20 cm away from the animal.
Observe respiratory movements and tissues for cyanosis during anesthesia.
Monitor cardiovascular function with capillary refill time.
Perform antisepsis with iopovidone iodine in a spiral pattern from center to periphery.
Trim hair around the surgical site (trichotomy).
Place sterile fields over the surgical area.
Insert four Sylastic® plates subcutaneously after sufficient dissection.
Suture the skin using nylon 4-0 USP suture material.
Apply an Elizabethan collar post-surgery to prevent the animal from removing sutures.
Harvest the implants along with the fibrous tissue.
Perform grafting using duralplasty.
Preoperative fasting for 12 hours if indicated.
Administer anesthesia with Propofol infusion (alternative anesthesia can be used).
Clean the area with povidone iodine in a spiral motion from the center to the periphery.
Perform trichotomy.
Establish sterile fields.
Maintain temperature control using 100 watt lamps at a distance of 20 cm.
Monitor respiratory function by observing breathing movements and looking for cyanosis.
Monitor cardiovascular function using capillary refill time.
Administer CPR if necessary, performing 5 compressions to 2 breaths (which may be done by pipetting air into the nostril of the animal).
Make a subcutaneous incision wider than needed to dissect the fibrous capsule and remove the implants.
Preserve the fibrous capsule at all costs during dissection.
Evert the edges of the incision.
Place the everted edges in physiological solution for later use.
Suture the incision with Nylon 4-0 USP.
Reposition the subject in ventral decubitus.
Perform a sagittal incision 5 cm long midline on the subject's head.
Remove subcutaneous tissue to expose the skull.
Place lidocaine locally (10 IU) using a spray from Unipharm Laboratories.
Scrape properly to expose the skull.
Perform an initial trepanation with a craniotome or dentist minidrill.
Irrigate the region constantly during craniotomy.
Keep the removed bone in saline.
Perform durotomy dimensions 1.5x1.5 cm and extract central dura.
Select thicker fibrous capsule as autologous graft.
Cut the graft to size of defect.
Suture the graft with 4 points on every corner using Neurolon® 7-0 USP or Nylon 7-0 UPS.
Suture edges continuously with single point.
Place gentamicin locally (2.5 mg/kg) in a single dose.
Carry out four drill holes to pass sutures and secure bone graft.
Secure the bone graft to the skull using drilled holes.
Close the skin with Nylon 4-0 USP.
Warm the subject between 27-30 °C for recovery from anesthesia without noise or stress-inducing factors.
Maintain same conditions until the subject recovers physiological state.
Place an Elizabethan collar on the animal once it has recovered its physiological state.
Remove the Elizabethan collar after 10 days.
Administer diclofenac at a dose of 50 mg/kg every 24 hours as needed for analgesia.
Administer buprenorphine at a dose of 0.01-0.05 mg/kg every 12 hours if signs of pain are present.
Monitor the animals for epileptic episodes, signs of infection, and CNS impairment.
Sacrifice the rat after 3 weeks.
Obtain histological sections of the graft tissue.
Compare the dura excised in a previous procedure with the current histological sections.
